cases.input:
This landed in my inbox saying it's from my hosting provider and wants me to update a card. Is it real? Headers below.

Delivered-To: me@example.org
Received: by 2002:a05:6402:1234:0:0:0:0 with SMTP id x1csp123456ejb;
        Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:14:02 -0700 (PDT)
ARC-Authentication-Results: i=1; mx.example.org; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=bounce-7731@mailer.example.net
Return-Path: <bounce-7731@mailer.example.net>
Received: from mta12.mailer.example.net (mta12.mailer.example.net. [198.51.100.24])
        by mx.example.org with ESMTPS id q9si2203
        for <me@example.org>; Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:14:02 -0700 (PDT)
Received-SPF: pass (example.org: domain of bounce-7731@mailer.example.net designates 198.51.100.24 as permitted sender) client-ip=198.51.100.24;
Authentication-Results: mx.example.org;
       dkim=pass header.i=@mailer.example.net header.s=s1 header.b=Qk3dTe9a;
       spf=pass (example.org: domain of bounce-7731@mailer.example.net designates 198.51.100.24 as permitted sender) smtp.mailfrom=bounce-7731@mailer.example.net;
       dmarc=fail (p=REJECT sp=REJECT dis=NONE) header.from=northwind-hosting.example.com
DKIM-Signature: v=1; a=rsa-sha256; c=relaxed/relaxed; d=mailer.example.net; s=s1; h=from:to:subject:date:message-id; bh=2jUSOH9NhtVGCQWNr9BrIAPreKQjO6Sn7XIkfJVOzv8=; b=Qk3dTe9aEXAMPLEONLYSIGNATUREVALUE
From: "Northwind Hosting Billing" <billing@northwind-hosting.example.com>
To: me@example.org
Subject: Action required: payment method expired
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:13:58 +0000
Message-ID: <20261019151358.7731@mailer.example.net>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
cases.expects: An ideal answer says this is almost certainly not legitimate, grounded in the headers: SPF and DKIM pass only for mailer.example.net, neither aligns with the northwind-hosting.example.com From domain, so DMARC fails under a reject policy. It keeps the pass/fail summary first, separates the RFC 5322 From from the RFC 5321 envelope sender, and does not trust the display name.

cases.input:
Run an email header analysis on this one. I need to know where SPF, DKIM, DMARC and ARC stand and whether the domains line up. It came through our team's mailing list.

Authentication-Results: mx.example.com;
       dkim=pass header.d=partner-example.com header.s=sel2026 header.b=Zr8mP1xA;
       spf=pass (mx.example.com: domain of bounce+lists=example.com@lists.partner-example.com designates 203.0.113.55 as permitted sender) smtp.mailfrom=bounce+lists=example.com@lists.partner-example.com;
       arc=pass (i=1 spf=pass spfdomain=partner-example.com dkim=pass dkdomain=partner-example.com dmarc=pass fromdomain=partner-example.com);
       dmarc=pass (p=QUARANTINE sp=QUARANTINE dis=NONE) header.from=partner-example.com
ARC-Seal: i=1; a=rsa-sha256; t=1792420511; cv=none; d=mx.example.com; s=arc-20260101; b=EXAMPLESEALVALUE
ARC-Message-Signature: i=1; a=rsa-sha256; c=relaxed/relaxed; d=mx.example.com; s=arc-20260101; h=from:to:subject:date; bh=EXAMPLEBODYHASH; b=EXAMPLEMSGSIG
ARC-Authentication-Results: i=1; mx.example.com; dkim=pass header.d=partner-example.com; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=bounce+lists=example.com@lists.partner-example.com; dmarc=pass header.from=partner-example.com
Received: from lists.partner-example.com (lists.partner-example.com [203.0.113.55])
        by mx.example.com with ESMTPS; Mon, 19 Oct 2026 14:35:11 +0000
Return-Path: <bounce+lists=example.com@lists.partner-example.com>
DKIM-Signature: v=1; a=rsa-sha256; c=relaxed/relaxed; d=partner-example.com; s=sel2026; h=from:to:subject:date:list-id; bh=EXAMPLEBH; b=Zr8mP1xAEXAMPLE
From: Priya Raman <priya@mail.partner-example.com>
To: team-all@example.com
Subject: [team-all] Q4 vendor review notes
List-Id: <team-all.lists.partner-example.com>
cases.expects: An ideal answer reports SPF, DKIM, DMARC and ARC all as pass, and correctly finds that relaxed alignment holds because the subdomain mail.partner-example.com shares the organizational domain partner-example.com with the DKIM d= value, while the envelope sender sits on a different list domain than the From. It notes the ARC chain has a single hop and says what that does and does not prove.

cases.input:
forwarded this to me from a colleague, she thinks it's phishing but says the mail client showed it as "verified". all I have is this chunk, the rest got cut off when she pasted it. what do you make of it

Received: from unknown (HELO mail-gw.example.net) (192.0.2.77)
  by mx.example.org with SMTP; 21 Oct 2026 02:41:19 +0000
Authentication-Results: mx.example.org; spf=pass smtp.mailfrom=ceo@acme-corp.example.com; dkim=pass header.d=acme-corp.example.com; dmarc=pass header.from=acme-corp.example.com
Received: from mail-gw.example.net (mail-gw.example.net [192.0.2.77])
  by mx.example.org (Postfix) with ESMTP id 4F2A81
Return-Path: <ceo@acme-corp.example.com>
From: "Marcus Hale (CEO)" <m.hale@acme-corp-payments.example.com>
Reply-To: m.hale.urgent@mailbox.example.net
To: finance@example.org
Subject: Wire needed today - confidential
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 02:40:55 +0000
Message-ID: <a81f@mail-gw.example.net>
X-Mailer: MassSender 4.2
[...truncated...]
cases.expects: An ideal answer refuses to take the pasted Authentication-Results at face value: it sits below the first Received line with no trusted receiving-host provenance beyond a claimed hostname, and the visible mismatch (From at acme-corp-payments.example.com, envelope and auth domain at acme-corp.example.com, Reply-To elsewhere) means the passes would not align. It says the truncation leaves ARC not present and key facts unknowable, avoids inventing results, and gives the checks that would settle it.
